Specific implementations like the "Two-rate field" generation optimize large-scale voxel planets by separating global and local octave evaluation [S3, unofficial].

The claim states that the 'Two-rate field' generation optimizes large-scale voxel planets by separating global and local octave evaluation. The evidence explicitly defines 'Two-rate field' as: 'continent- and range-wide octaves are evaluated at lattice nodes and blended.' In the context of procedural generation, 'continent- and range-wide' corresponds to global/large-scale evaluation, while the blending implies combining these with local details (implied by the 'two-rate' nature and the optimization context). The evidence also confirms performance improvements (optimization) from 41–43 µs to 32–34 µs per tile. Therefore, the facts in the claim are supported by the evidence.
